solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very rich plant producing wagons and things

parts.note: someone 'rolling in it' or just 'rolling' is very wealthy
stock is a garden flower, a sweet-scented plant

explanation.surface: A wealthy factory owner turns out carts and assorted goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory making the wagons, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers all the wheeled vehicles a railway owns: wagons, carriages and locomotives.

clue.text: Tease players, offering achievement award

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
a band is a group of musicians playing together

explanation.surface: Mocking the musicians while handing them a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon worn to show a distinction such as a medal or prize; this is an old spelling.

clue.text: Crown representative's lad involved with union letter

indicators.note: involved means entangled or mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man sends a letter about a trade union to the monarch's agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link ('is'); 'with' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain he is the monarch's personal representative in each county.

clue.text: Picturesque scene over in Caerphilly district

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse order
in means the letters are found within the words Caerphilly district

explanation.surface: A pretty view across a Welsh area.
explanation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a town in South Wales. 'in' takes LLYDI from inside 'Caerphilly district' and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral, peaceful rural view or scene is what this kind of poem portrays.

clue.text: Green bird born in French island

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: île is French for island

explanation.surface: A green seabird hatched on a French island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the bird's colour but means naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone green is inexperienced and naive, easily tricked or fooled.

clue.text: Express disapproval over posh ballerina's skirt

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
U means upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Tutting at a smart ballet dancer's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link meaning 'about'; U for upper class comes from the 1950s U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The short stiff layered net costume classic dancers wear on stage.

clue.text: Copy poster principally offering cheap diamond

parts.note: a carbon is a carbon copy
an ad, an advertisement, can be a poster

indicators.note: principally means first, so the opening letter of offering is taken

explanation.surface: A copied advert mainly selling a cut-price gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A black, impure industrial diamond, valued for drilling rather than jewellery.

clue.text: Gang leader's girl touring cool part of France

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the outer pieces surround the other

parts.note: Al Capone was the archetypal gang leader, so his name with the 's gives ALS
Lorraine is a woman's name
ace is slang for excellent or cool

explanation.surface: A mobster's girlfriend travelling round a pleasant French region.
explanation.definitionFit: This region in north-east France was annexed by Germany in 1871.

clue.text: Wherefore, reportedly, sci-fi writer briefly identifies winged dragon

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard said, so a word's sound is used

parts.note: wherefore means why

indicators.note: briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Jules Verne was a pioneering science fiction writer

explanation.surface: Why, people say, a science fiction author depicts a flying monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic beast with two legs, wings and a barbed tail, a kind of dragon.

clue.text: Strapping lad initially housed in part of Gt Manchester

indicators.note: something housed in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word lad

explanation.surface: A big strong young man living in a Manchester town.
explanation.walkthrough: BURY is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapping person is big and well built, sturdy and muscular.

clue.text: Having limited calories, get better? Exactly

parts.note: lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie food
to rally is to recover from illness

explanation.surface: A dieter asks whether eating fewer calories will make them well, and is told: precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, the adverb means precisely or word for word, so it can stand for 'exactly'.

clue.text: University invested in Lamb's complete essays? Praise be!

indicators.note: invested in means placed within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: complete gives ALL and Charles Lamb's essays are the Essays of Elia, giving ELIA

explanation.surface: A university puts money into Charles Lamb's collected works, and someone gives thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb, the English essayist, wrote under the pen name Elia; 'invested in' puts U between ALL and ELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a liturgical cry of praise to God, Hebrew for 'praise ye the Lord'.

clue.text: It may be paid in, including silver

indicators.note: including means one piece contains the other

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Something paid in, along with silver coins, like a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid in' looks like a banking phrase, but 'in' belongs to the wordplay; the definition is 'It may be paid', as in paying respect.
explanation.definitionFit: One pays tribute or respect to someone, a fixed phrase in which it is the thing paid.

clue.text: Medic, female, penning article in a brown study

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Emily is a woman's name
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman doctor writing a piece while lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown study is a state of absorbed reverie, so acting in one is acting in a daydreaming way.

clue.text: English cricketer ultimately caught by Germans out for a duck

indicators.note: caught by means held within the other piece
out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of cricketer

explanation.surface: An English batsman out for a duck to German bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, but here 'duck' is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating diving bird with a slender hooked bill, a type of waterfowl.

clue.text: After most of race, men finally keel over

indicators.note: after places the last piece behind the first
most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to career is to rush along at speed, to race

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word men

explanation.surface: Runners collapse near the end of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that tips over onto its side heels or lurches, which is what keeling over means.

clue.text: Bread? It's served up with tea and a little butter

parts.note: cha, or char, is British slang for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reversed, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish served with tea and a dab of butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat unleavened Indian bread is one example of bread; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Fully-developed horse bearing 5? Not half!

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the horse holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word is kept, the other dropped

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer to 5 down, the ballet skirt

explanation.surface: A grown horse carrying a ballerina's skirt, absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it halves the 5-down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grown or ripe has reached full development, an adult stage.

clue.text: Woman crossing ends of fields much like the Fens

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name

indicators.note: ends of points to the last letters of fields and much

explanation.surface: A woman walking over fields in the waterlogged Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying, once swampy land in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The region was boggy wetland before drainage, so it is wet and boggy.

clue.text: Drive away racecourse spy in exchange of fire

parts.note: shoo is to drive animals or people off
a tout spies on racehorses in training to sell tips

explanation.surface: Chasing off a man snooping at the races leads to gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is someone who watches racehorses in training and sells tips on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfight between two sides is a decisive battle with guns, a firefight.

clue.text: Organ originally borne on large farm cart

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach, an organ

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of borne

parts.note: re means on or about

explanation.surface: A church instrument first carried on a big farm wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled tipping cart used on farms, later famous for carrying the condemned in Paris.

clue.text: Endlessly regret method securing new airport facility

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the outer pieces enclose another
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a way is a method

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the way a new airport amenity was built.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports have long strips where planes take off and land.

clue.text: Colourful band finally uses guitarist's aid left out

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word uses
out means the given letter is removed

parts.note: a plectrum is a pick for plucking guitar strings

explanation.surface: A rock group ends up using a guitar pick but leaves it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' reads as a music group, but it is a range of colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Light split by a prism forms a band of colours running from red to violet.

clue.text: Copper bar from a Caribbean island

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A copper ingot from somewhere in the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to Havana's country, the largest island of the West Indies.

clue.text: Head off unspecified fever

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: something unspecified is vague

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop an unidentified illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for malarial fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: Back a great deal, showing wisdom after the event

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs
a sight is informal for a lot, as in 'a sight better'

explanation.surface: Reflecting at length afterwards brings a lot of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding a situation only after it has happened is the classic definition of knowing too late.

clue.text: Thorny shrub, one accommodated by Remus's brother

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed inside the other piece

parts.note: in Uncle Remus's tales animals are called Brer, a dialect form of brother
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prickly bush that gave lodging to Romulus's twin.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus suggests Romulus, but it is Uncle Remus, narrator of the Brer Rabbit stories.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a prickly bush such as the wild rose, also the heather whose root makes pipes.

clue.text: Source of water distributed later in Wales

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Water to be supplied later across Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore into a confined aquifer where pressure pushes groundwater up without pumping.
